P03-019.boundary_rationale: Onset side: MT 18:27 opens with no formula device, וּבְשׁ֣וּב רָשָׁ֗ע מֵֽרִשְׁעָתוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.18.27) ('again, when a wicked person turns from the wickedness he has committed'), the positive repentance case answering 18:24-26; the running text reads the ketiv וישוב (oshb:Ezek.18.28) at 18:28. Israel's objection recurs at 18:29, where the OSHB editors' note records a form of questionable validity kept as the Leningrad Codex and BHS have it (single witness). The judgment proper then opens at 18:30 with לָכֵן֩ אִ֨ישׁ כִּדְרָכָ֜יו אֶשְׁפֹּ֤ט אֶתְכֶם֙ בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.18.30) (“Therefore I will judge you, house of Israel, everyone according to his ways," says the Lord Yahweh”, web:Ezek.18.30); the quoted run ends on the utterance formula, which stands mid-verse in 18:30 and is not itself the onset device. Close side: the row runs to the chapter's own end, 18:32, whose final clause וְהָשִׁ֖יבוּ וִֽחְיֽוּ (oshb:Ezek.18.32) ('so turn, and live') closes the chapter, matched by a pe recorded on this same verse; the utterance formula recurs mid-verse there rather than at the very end, so what carries this close is the chapter-final imperative clause, corroborated by the pe recorded on the verse and by the qinah command that opens at 19:1, a licensed onset on the far face. This row's onset, by contrast, is a case turn inside one word-event unit: 18:27 opens the positive case with no formula of its own, and the samekh recorded after 18:26 behind it corroborates the turn without deciding it. An onset seam of that shape, against a close that is two-faced, is the ground of the row's medium_low.

P06-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:1 opens with the word-event formula, "וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.25.1) — the strict 39-form and the any-form 41-count both, carrying no dateline. In the WEB, “Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.25.1). 25:2 supplies the addressee, "בֶּן אָדָ֕ם שִׂ֥ים פָּנֶ֖יךָ אֶל בְּנֵ֣י עַמּ֑וֹן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.2) — the set-your-face command “toward the children of Ammon” (web:Ezek.25.2, WEB) is the first of the book's set-your-face verses (sweep: 9 verses) to name a foreign nation, and the class shift that opens the oracles-against-the-nations collection; Ammon itself is not a new addressee here, since the sword oracle at MT 21:33 (= WEB 21:28) already concerns the children of Ammon. Close (weighed from both sides): 25:7 ends "לָכֵ֡ן הִנְנִי֩ נָטִ֨יתִי אֶת יָדִ֜י עָלֶ֗יךָ וּנְתַתִּ֤יךָֽ לבג לַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְהִכְרַתִּ֨יךָ֙ מִן הָ֣עַמִּ֔ים וְהַאֲבַדְתִּ֖יךָ מִן הָאֲרָצ֑וֹת אַשְׁמִ֣ידְךָ֔ וְיָדַעְתָּ֖ כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.7; לבג there is the verse’s ketiv, Qere לְבַז֙), closing on the 2ms recognition variant "and you shall know that I am YHWH" with a SAMEKH immediately after. An earlier internal close sits at 25:5, "וְנָתַתִּ֤י אֶת רַבָּה֙ לִנְוֵ֣ה גְמַלִּ֔ים וְאֶת בְּנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹן לְמִרְבַּץ צֹ֑אן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ם כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.5), which also ends on a 2mp recognition-family clause (the wider 2mp recognition family, sweep: 21 verses, includes 25:5, not the strict 2ms list, sweep: 5 verses) and carries its own SAMEKH. Because a refrain closes the unit before it, both 25:5 and 25:7 are treated as closes; they are kept in one row because 25:6 reopens with a coordinating messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה", oshb:Ezek.25.6) against the same addressee (Ammon) rather than a fresh nation, so no addressee-class shift separates 25:5 from 25:7. Ahead of this row, 25:8 opens a fresh messenger formula with an addressee change to Moab, the row's forward hard seam.

P02-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.1 וַתִּשָּׂ֨א אֹתִ֜י ר֗וּחַ וַתָּבֵ֣א אֹ֠תִי אֶל שַׁ֨עַר בֵּית יְהוָ֤ה הַקַּדְמוֹנִי֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה קָדִ֔ימָה וְהִנֵּה֙ בְּפֶ֣תַח הַשַּׁ֔עַר עֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אִ֑ישׁ וָאֶרְאֶ֨ה בְתוֹכָ֜ם אֶת יַאֲזַנְיָ֧ה בֶן עַזֻּ֛ר וְאֶת פְּלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖הוּ שָׂרֵ֖י הָעָֽם — a fresh transport (“the Spirit lifted me up and brought me” (web:Ezek.11.1)) to the east gate, introducing new participants (Jaazaniah son of Azzur, Pelatiah son of Benaiah). The witness records a pe after 11:1 (single-witness); it stands inside the row, disclosed and not cut, as the pe after 11:6 is. The onset itself rests on the transport at 11:1, a predicate-class member carrying two tokens, while the far face behind it, 10:22, carries no mark and no formula; the witness records no section mark anywhere in chapter 10, and the pe following 11:1 stands inside the row, not at its onset seam. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.13 וַֽיְהִי֙ כְּהִנָּ֣בְאִ֔י וּפְלַטְיָ֥הוּ בֶן בְּנָיָ֖ה מֵ֑ת וָאֶפֹּ֨ל עַל פָּנַ֜י וָאֶזְעַ֣ק קוֹל גָּד֗וֹל וָאֹמַר֙ אֲהָהּ֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה כָּלָה֙ אַתָּ֣ה עֹשֶׂ֔ה אֵ֖ת שְׁאֵרִ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל — Pelatiah's death and the prophet's cry “Ah Lord Yahweh! Will you make a full end of the remnant of Israel?” (web:Ezek.11.13) — is a narrative close; a pe follows this verse as well (single-witness), and that mark is this close seam's corroboration. Both sides: the courtyard scene runs as one continuous unit from the transport to the prophet's cry, with a sub-onset at oshb:Ezek.11.5 “Yahweh's Spirit fell on me, and he said to me” (web:Ezek.11.5) that introduces direct judgment speech but carries no word-event formula and is not itself an addressee-class shift, so it is disclosed as internal texture rather than a competing row seam. Both near faces are licensed -- the transport at 11:1, the narrative close at 11:13 with its pe -- while the onset's far face is bare; the row's medium is the record of that one bare face.

P10-014.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 43:13 opens with an explicit topic header, וְאֵ֨לֶּה מִדּ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֨חַ֙ (oshb:Ezek.43.13), the vav-initial “these are the measurements of the altar” (web:Ezek.43.13), functioning as a list-onset in the same way such headers do elsewhere in the book, immediately after the doubled inclusio that closes 43:12. The row descends through the altar's base, lower and greater ledges, hearth and horns, in cubit-and-handbreadth units; 43:15 carries two editors' notes and no K/Q note (one marks an anomalous form, the other records a ketiv/qere abandoned or added relative to BHS, in agreement with the Leningrad Codex; single-witness), and the span's one K/Q note stands at 43:16. Close side: 43:17 ends with the steps 'toward the east' before 43:18 opens with the messenger formula, a clean tier-1 onset on the far side even though this row's own close rests on content completion rather than a refrain.
P10-014.device_notes: No parashah mark in this row. One K/Q verse is disclosed: 43:16 carries a K/Q note on the altar-hearth term, whose ketiv and Qere spell the same letters in a different order (single-witness); the disputed reading is the noun itself, not a numeral, so no measurement figure is under dispute although the verse gives the hearth as twelve by twelve. the notes at 43:15 are editors' notes, not K/Q notes: one marks an anomalous form, the other records a ketiv/qere abandoned or added relative to BHS, and neither is argued as boundary evidence. No paseq touches 43:13-43:17.

P11-007.device_notes: Ezek.46.1 and Ezek.46.6 carry the construction glossed 'the new moon'; Ezek.46.3 carries 'at the new moons' -- all disclosed as the book's chodesh-root homograph family, none a date formula. Ezek.46.13 ('a lamb of its first year') carries a year word explicitly NOT a dateline, disclosed to forestall misreading. The samekh recorded after Ezek.46.11 is single-witness texture, disclosed and non-cutting. This row's 15-verse length sits at the top of the measured/listed-block cap (14-16), disclosed. Ezek.45.25 is followed by a samekh (single witness), corroborating the onset at Ezek.46.1. The close verse is also a K/Q site: at oshb:Ezek.46.15 the running text keeps the ketiv ועשו, and the note's Qere reads יַעֲשׂ֨וּ (single-witness); no boundary is argued from either form.

P02-001.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.8.1 opens with the dateline וַיְהִ֣י בַּשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשִּׁשִּׁ֗ית בַּשִּׁשִּׁי֙ בַּחֲמִשָּׁ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ אֲנִי֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בְּבֵיתִ֔י וְזִקְנֵ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה יוֹשְׁבִ֣ים לְפָנָ֑י וַתִּפֹּ֤ל עָלַי֙ שָׁ֔ם יַ֖ד אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהֹוִֽה (sixth year, sixth month, fifth day) carrying the hand-of-YHWH idiom in its אדני יהוה form (tier-1 vision onset; the construct-only sweep counts 7 hand-of-YHWH verses book-wide, of which this is the only one carrying the double divine name), immediately followed by the transport at oshb:Ezek.8.3 וַיִּשְׁלַח֙ תַּבְנִ֣ית יָ֔ד וַיִּקָּחֵ֖נִי בְּצִיצִ֣ת רֹאשִׁ֑י וַתִּשָּׂ֣א אֹתִ֣י ר֣וּחַ בֵּֽין הָאָ֣רֶץ וּבֵ֣ין הַשָּׁמַ֡יִם וַתָּבֵא֩ אֹתִ֨י יְרוּשָׁלְַ֜מָה בְּמַרְא֣וֹת אֱלֹהִ֗ים אֶל פֶּ֜תַח שַׁ֤עַר הַפְּנִימִית֙ הַפּוֹנֶ֣ה צָפ֔וֹנָה אֲשֶׁר שָׁ֣ם מוֹשַׁ֔ב סֵ֖מֶל הַקִּנְאָ֥ה הַמַּקְנֶֽה (the Spirit lifts the prophet and sets him at Jerusalem's inner-court gate — a transport verse of the book's counted guided-motion class, sweep: 33 verses book-wide) and the phrase במראות אלהים 'in visions of God' (sweep: 3 verses book-wide — 1:1, 8:3, 40:2, the three vision-transport frames). A pe follows MT 7:27 (single witness), the paragraph mark standing behind this unit's onset at 8:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.8.6 ends the directed “lift up your eyes” (web:Ezek.8.5) scene with וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י בֶּן אָדָ֕ם הֲרֹאֶ֥ה אַתָּ֖ה מהם (ketiv; qere מָ֣ה הֵ֣ם) עֹשִׂ֑ים תּוֹעֵב֨וֹת גְּדֹל֜וֹת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל עֹשִׂ֣ים פֹּ֗ה לְרָֽחֳקָה֙ מֵעַ֣ל מִקְדָּשִׁ֔י וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה תּוֹעֵב֖וֹת גְּדֹלֽוֹת, the prophet's first sight of “the seat of the image of jealousy” (web:Ezek.8.3) and the promise “you will again see yet other great abominations.” (web:Ezek.8.6), which turns the page to the next scene rather than closing the vision; a samekh follows oshb:Ezek.8.6 (single-witness), giving Masoretic corroboration to a seam here even though no oracle-refrain formula is present. Both sides: the onset side is triple-marked (dateline, hand, transport) and is the strongest onset in the book; the close side rests on the samekh plus the forward-pointing 'again see' formula rather than a recognition or utterance refrain, so the row is held below high confidence.

P11-009.device_notes: MT 46.22 carries seven U+05C4 puncta-extraordinaria combining marks in the verse's own bytes, single-witness. A row splicing this verse carries the marks in its own quoted bytes -- that is source-true, not degradation, and U+05C4 is treated as a legitimate combining mark, not corruption. Both transport verses here belong to the book's counted guided-motion class (sweep: 33 verses): Ezek.46.19 at the onset, and Ezek.46.21, which opens with two such verbs, וַיּוֹצִיאֵ֗נִי and וַיַּ֣עֲבִירֵ֔נִי (oshb:Ezek.46.21), 'he brought me out ... and made me pass', an intra-row transport sub-onset at which the row does not cut. The samekh recorded after Ezek.46.19 is single-witness, mid-unit, non-cutting.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “the building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), the notice “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26) 'and “the side rooms of the” (web:Ezek.41.26) house, and the thresholds' immediately before 42:1's double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי (oshb:Ezek.42.1), moves the tour out to the outer court -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset is tier-1 even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. The puncta extraordinaria at 41:20, וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ (oshb:Ezek.41.20), five instances of the upper dot U+05C4, are disclosed single-witness as intra-row texture on the decorative program's own close, not as boundary evidence.

P01-013.device_notes: Five-verse unit; justified by the fresh messenger-formula onset at 7:5 and the doubled-refrain recognition close at 7:9 (shared with 7:4), not by size. Disclosed as short, not capped. Marks in three directions, MEASURED in this witness (single-witness) on its convention that a mark is recorded ON the verse it follows: onset seam — a pe is recorded on MT 7:4, so the witness breaks immediately before this row's first verse; interior 7:5-7:8 — no mark; close seam — no samekh and no pe is recorded on MT 7:9. The witness's own sectioning, read against this row: the next mark after the pe on MT 7:4 is the pe on MT 7:22, so the witness's own open section runs 7:5-7:22 and this row's close at 7:9 falls inside it. That sectioning corroborates the longer rival rather than this row, and it is disclosed for the alternative it corroborates. It does not unseat the row: a section boundary of the witness is weak corroboration that never outranks a licensed text signal, and the near face of this close carries one — the 2mp recognition clause at 7:9, whose only word after the formula is the dependent participle מַכֶּֽה (MEASURED: the consonantal skeleton carries וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה at characters 63-80 of 84, counting from 1 with both ends included, with מַכֶּֽה filling the remainder), so it is verse-final in effect and grades as an ordinary licensed near-face signal rather than the weak mid-verse shape. The absence of a mark at 7:9 is disclosed and is never read as counter-evidence (oshb:Ezek.7.9).
P01-013.boundary_rationale: Onset: 7:5 reopens with a fresh messenger formula immediately after 7:4's pe-marked recognition close — כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה (oshb:Ezek.7.5) “The Lord Yahweh says: 'A disaster! A unique disaster! Behold, it comes.” (web:Ezek.7.5). Close: 7:9, the 2mp recognition-family close carrying an appended participle, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה (oshb:Ezek.7.9) “Then you will know that I, Yahweh, strike.” (web:Ezek.7.9); this recognition member also carries the doubled “my eye will not spare” (web:Ezek.7.4) refrain — MEASURED at 5 verses book-wide (5:11, 7:4, 7:9, 8:18, 9:10) by a consonantal-skeleton sweep of the phrase *lo tachos eini* over the pointed Hebrew witness, the WEB contracting the clause at every one of those verses except 7:4, which is why the delimited five-word run is referenced to web:Ezek.7.4 — the same refrain the close at 7:4 already carries, so 7:9 closes a distinct short unit before the unmarked doom-poem reopens at 7:10 with no formula of its own.

P02-016.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.1 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, a strict word-event formula, opens the oracle against the false (male) prophets; the messenger formula opens the speech proper at oshb:Ezek.13.3 and again at oshb:Ezek.13.8. MT 12:28 is followed by a samekh (single witness), corroborating this unit's onset at 13:1. Close: oshb:Ezek.13.9 וְהָיְתָ֣ה יָדִ֗י אֶֽל הַנְּבִיאִ֞ים הַחֹזִ֣ים שָׁוְא֮ וְהַקֹּסְמִ֣ים כָּזָב֒ בְּס֧וֹד עַמִּ֣י לֹֽא יִהְי֗וּ וּבִכְתָ֤ב בֵּֽית יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֹ֣א יִכָּתֵ֔בוּ וְאֶל אַדְמַ֥ת יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֣א יָבֹ֑אוּ וִידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends “Then you will know that I am the Lord Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.9) — a recognition-formula variant carrying the longer divine name אדני יהוה rather than the plain יהוה of the counted 28- and 21-verse recognition families; this is a counted class in its own right, the adonai-form recognition close (sweep: 5 verses — MT 13:9, 23:49, 24:24, 28:24, 29:16), every one of them verse-final and none of them a member of the 28-verse or the 21-verse family. MEASURED against the pointed Hebrew witness the clause וידעתם כי אני אדני יהוה ends MT 13:9 (on the consonantal skeleton, characters 109-131 of 131, counted from 1 with both ends included), so this close carries a licensed verse-final close-role signal, and the counts are still never blended. Both sides: against a strict word-event onset with a doubled messenger formula (13:3, 13:8) and a verse-final recognition close, what holds this row short of high is the far side of the close seam, not the divine-name form: oshb:Ezek.13.10 opens יען וביען and carries no word-event, messenger, set-your-face or transport onset, and this witness records no samekh or pe on MT 13:9 (single-witness; this chapter's marks fall on 13:7, 13:12, 13:16 and 13:19), so the far face of this close is empty, and a licensed near face against an empty far face is what the row's medium records.

P02-006.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating 10:9-17 as texture inside a larger 10:1-22 (or 10:1-11:13) row rather than its own row was the live alternative and is the reason this row is held at low rather than medium confidence: nothing in the book's formula inventory marks 10:9 as an onset, and the wheel material could just as defensibly be folded into the adjacent units at Ezek.10.1-10.8 or Ezek.10.18-10.22. It is kept as its own row because it is a bytes-verifiable, self-contained descriptive block (the wheel vocabulary אוֹפַ֣ן (oshb:Ezek.10.9) and הַגַּלְגַּ֖ל (oshb:Ezek.10.13) clusters in 10:6-17 and 1:15-21 but is not confined to them: the wheel noun also stands at 3:13, 10:19 and 11:22, and the companion term at 10:2, 23:24 and 26:10) bounded by narrated action on both sides.

P04-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a second time at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17, which the WEB renders “Cry and wail, son of man”, was considered and rejected. That verse carries the son-of-man address, one of the 93 verses in that class, and carries no word-event and no messenger formula; the WEB opens no paragraph at it, and translation lineation would not drive a boundary in any case. A further seam was weighed one verse later, from both sides. The verse closing at web:Ezek.21.13 = oshb:Ezek.21.18 ends on the utterance formula (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה), “says the Lord Yahweh”, with a pe following it in this witness (single witness); the next verse, web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, opens with the ve'attah, the and-you address “You therefore, son of man, prophesy” (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א). Both sides carry real evidence: an utterance-formula close on one side of the seam and, on the other, the ve'attah, an onset-class device that brings the son-of-man address with it. That signature is verse-final, its verse being one of the 81 in the long utterance class, so the second limb of the sub-onset test is met on the bytes here and is not denied. What carries the unit past the seam is the shape of the renewal: a ve'attah that renews the command to prophesy to the same addressee, standing after a verse-final utterance signature, is a paragraph and not an onset. The ve'attah is new at MT 21:19, but the address it renews is not: the son-of-man address with the command to prophesy already stands at web:Ezek.21.9 = oshb:Ezek.21.14, where it introduces the book's only messenger formula naming the Lord alone, כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י, and the son-of-man address returns at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17; and MT 21:19 continues the same sword doubled a third time (וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙, oshb:Ezek.21.19), the sword already sharpened and polished at oshb:Ezek.21.14-16, rather than opening a new topic.

P05-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: The live rival is a seam at 24:24/24:25, and it carries evidence on both faces. Its far face, 24:24, ends verse-final on the adonai-form recognition clause, וִֽידַעְתֶּ֕ם כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.24.24), a member of that counted class (sweep: 5 verses), and this witness records a samekh after the verse (single-witness). Its near face, 24:25, opens with the ve'attah, וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם (oshb:Ezek.24.25), a son-of-man address that turns from the house of Israel to the prophet himself, so the addressee changes there. The row holds across that seam on the sign inclusio: 24:24 names Ezekiel a sign to the people (לְמוֹפֵ֔ת, oshb:Ezek.24.24), and 24:27 closes by naming him that sign again (לְמוֹפֵ֔ת, oshb:Ezek.24.27), so 24:25-27 completes the sign the unit set up rather than opening a unit of its own.

P08-011.boundary_rationale: Onset: a fresh messenger formula at Ezek.36.13 כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֚עַן אֹמְרִ֣ים לָכֶ֔ם אֹכֶ֥לֶת אָדָ֖ם אתי וּמְשַׁכֶּ֥לֶת גויך הָיִֽית (oshb:Ezek.36.13) opens immediately after the refrain-grade close and samekh mark at oshb:Ezek.36.12, itself licensed as a cutting seam by the addressee change from the 2mp/2ms address of Ezek.36.1-Ezek.36.12 (‘you,’ the mountains) to the 2fs address (‘you,’ feminine singular, the land) that opens here — satisfying the seam condition from this side as well as from the close side ('a seam is assessed from both sides'). MT 36.13 and MT 36.14 are BOTH doubled-note K/Q verses (two Qere each): oshb:Ezek.36.13 carries ketiv 'אתי' / qere 'אָ֑תְּ' (‘you,’ feminine singular) and ketiv 'גויך' / qere 'גּוֹיַ֖יִךְ' ('your nation' plene); oshb:Ezek.36.14 carries ketiv 'וגויך' / qere 'וְגוֹיַ֖יִךְ' and ketiv 'תכשלי' / qere 'תְשַׁכְּלִי'. Of those four notes, morpheme separators are present in the K/Q layer -- and therefore stripped in the forms as rendered here -- only for the SECOND 36:13 note (2 separators) and the FIRST 36:14 note (4); the first 36:13 note and the second 36:14 note carry none in the layer at all, so nothing was stripped from either of them. MEASURED by counting the '/' separators in each note: 36:13 gives 0 and 2, 36:14 gives 4 and 0. Ezek.36.14 also carries the utterance formula, and it recurs at Ezek.36.15 וְלֹא אַשְׁמִ֨יעַ אֵלַ֤יִךְ עוֹד֙ כְּלִמַּ֣ת הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וְחֶרְפַּ֥ת עַמִּ֖ים לֹ֣א תִשְׂאִי ע֑וֹד וגויך לֹא תַכְשִׁ֣לִי ע֔וֹד נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.36.15) (itself carrying one more K/Q pair on 'your nation', its ketiv spelled as at oshb:Ezek.36.14 and, without the conjunction, as at oshb:Ezek.36.13) — a doubled internal utterance close. Close: a samekh mark follows Ezek.36.15, ending this sub-unit before the fresh, formally distinct word-event of Ezek.36.16.
